desc: Dusk café façade (teaser): one by one, a violet thought window pops above every patron ("what EVERYONE was thinking").
Café table: a girl leans in, thinking "I copied her homework." (a secret); her friend says "I'm fine!" while thinking "I'm SO not fine." (a lie).
A girl on a bench steals a glance at the boy beside her; a pink thought: "He's kinda cute..." (what your crush actually thinks).
MONDAY chip. The alarm rings at 7:00; Noah's eyes snap open and he sits up in bed in warm morning light.
Close-up: violet rings ripple out from Noah's head as he realises something is different ("exactly that power").
Morning: the same café in daylight; Noah, sleepy, walks in for his coffee.
Over Noah's shoulder: the smiling barista slides a ceramic mug toward him — "Here you go! Have a great day!" — and his hand reaches in.
The barista keeps smiling (mouth closed) while her thought appears beside her head: "Please don't spill it. Please don't spill it." — the mug starts to slip from her fingers.
Extreme close-up of Noah's face: his eyes snap wide and the falling mug is reflected in them ("WHAT THE—").
Low-angle slow motion: the ceramic mug tumbles past Noah's reaching silhouette (right), time FREEZES with a violet pulse, then resumes.
Floor level, the barista's feet behind: the ceramic mug smashes — coffee splash, shards scatter.
The barista stares down at the mess, hands clutched to her chest; thought: "I'm getting fired."
Title card in the dusk sky above the café: "WHAT IF YOU COULD HEAR EVERYONE'S THOUGHTS?" (bold, glowing, fully opaque).
3/4 medium shot: outside the café, Noah stumbles against the window clutching his head; faint whispers swirl ("losing his mind").
Noah's point of view through the café window: the patrons' thoughts fade in one after another.
Wide: Noah steps out onto the busy morning street.
Slightly high angle over the crowd: a readable thought window pops over every passer-by in sequence ("EVERY single person around him").
Side-tracking: a businessman on his phone strides past Noah — "Yes, boss. Almost at the office."
Push in on the businessman: his thought window shows his boss tapping a foot beside a clock — "I'm still twenty minutes away."
Front-on, slightly low: a woman walks toward camera; her window shows a glowing oven — "Did I leave the oven on?"
Snap zoom onto a man in a flat cap staring right back at Noah: "Why is that kid staring at me?"
Close-up: Noah's disbelief turns into a grin — "Oh my god. This is actually real."
Morning, NORTHVIEW HIGH: students head inside; Noah walks in beside his best friend Leo (green cap), looking smug.
Classroom: Noah (back row, right) taps his temple smugly next to Leo; small thoughts pop above bored classmates ("anything he wanted").
From Noah's desk (his shoulder blurred, right): the teacher points — "Noah. What's the answer to question seven?"
Reverse from the front of the class: Noah freezes at his desk, nervous — "Uh..." — Leo glances at him.
The room drains of colour except Noah; the teacher's thought "Please don't say C again. It's B." — a glowing B detaches and flies across the room to hover over Noah's desk.
Low angle from desk height: Noah's hand shoots up — "B!"
Smash cut: the teacher, stunned — "...Correct."
Three-cut montage, each a new angle with a glowing answer ("x = 7", "1776", "H₂O"); it ends with Noah and Leo fist-bumping (VO: school wasn't so difficult).
Insert: the classroom clock's minute hand snaps to 12 (3:00) and the clock shakes as the bell rings.
3/4 hallway with lockers receding and window light on the floor: Noah strolls in, cocky.
Over Noah's shoulder down the hallway: small thoughts pop over students as he scans them ("more than anyone").
One-point corridor: Maya alone in a warm pool of light at the far end, holding her books; the label MAYA holds on screen.
Comedic: Noah hides behind an open locker door and peeks out nervously (too scared to talk to her for a year).
Long-lens push from behind Noah toward Maya; focus racks from Noah to Maya as the distance compresses.
Maya (books held to her chest) glances over; a pink handwritten thought with tiny hearts: "Wait... Noah actually looks kinda cute today."
Noah's eyes go wide — whispers "No way" — then a triumphant double fist-pump with sparkles.
Maya tilts her head, puzzled; a cooler blue thought: "Why is he smiling like that?"
Hard cut: Noah freezes into a painfully awkward grin, rubs his neck and looks away — "Oh." (record scratch).
Noah struts down the 3/4 hallway toward camera with sparkles — "luckiest person alive".
Low angle: Leo passes and the two best friends slap a high-five mid-stride.
From behind Noah: he walks up and pushes the CAFETERIA double doors open — warm light and a crowd spill out toward camera.
Locked behind Noah in a deep perspective cafeteria: every student has a thought shape over their head; they multiply and overlap.
Noah, worried ("Wait, hold on—"), as overlapping thought windows crowd in; camera pushes into them until violet fills the screen.
Orbit: Noah alone in a violet spotlight; thought panels hang on three depth layers and slide past at different speeds ("one person's thoughts was amazing").
Top-down over the cafeteria: long tables, a thought window rises over every head; a counter ticks up to "200 THOUGHTS".
Close-up: Noah, arms crossed, deadpan and wincing, boxed in by thought windows ("Not so much.").
Students on a bench at a cafeteria table, mouths shut, thoughts popping: "I'm starving." / "Why did she leave me on read?" / "I hate Mondays."
High 3/4 angle down a long table: one thought after another — "Did I fail chemistry?" / "Does anyone even like me?" / "Is my hair weird today?" …
Dutch high angle: tiny Noah in the spotlight below a sea of different thoughts ("Everyone was thinking something different").
The orbit tightens on Noah hugging himself as panels multiply around him ("couldn't turn ANY of it off").
Overload peak, three fast cuts: ECU of Noah's eyes, top-down of his hands pressed on his head, overhead of countless windows — then a hard cut to black silence.
3/4 medium shot in a quiet corridor: Noah presses his hands over his ears ("He tried covering his ears").
Profile extreme close-up: his hand clamped over his ear while violet thought-lines pass straight through it ("Nothing.").
Profile: Noah jams on huge headphones; the thought lines pass straight through them ("Still nothing.").
Wide symmetrical bathroom under one cold light: Noah alone in the centre while glowing thought windows drift straight through the walls.
Low angle: Noah throws his fists up and yells at the ceiling — "ARE YOU KIDDING ME?"
Afternoon, the hallway calm again (no effects): Noah slumps at his open locker, exhausted.
Insert: a photo taped inside the locker — Noah and Leo aged 8 (smaller, kid-sized), laughing: "best friends forever (age 8)".
Two-shot: Leo strolls in and taps Noah's shoulder — "Yo, you coming over Friday?"
Close on Noah as the hallway darkens; a violet thought window — its tail running to Leo's blurred cap in the right foreground — reveals word by word: "I can't keep doing this."
Down the corridor axis over Leo's shoulder: Noah asks "...Doing what?" — Leo, caught out: "What?"
Close on Leo, looking down, unaware Noah can hear: "I have to tell him. He's gonna hate me." — then a held silence.
Noah at his desk, chin in hand, worried; Leo's two thoughts drift around him as faded violet memory windows.
Library: Leo is looking at a page with a blue crest ("A") on his laptop and slams it shut as Noah walks up ("Was Leo planning to ditch him?").
Over Noah's shoulder: Leo laughs into his phone, spots Noah, and quickly hangs up and pockets it with an awkward smile ("lying this whole time?").
Slow push on Noah leaning around a corner to eavesdrop; faint thought-noise at the frame edges ("the more Noah listened...").
High angle down at the lockers: Leo grabs his bag with Noah hovering behind; Leo's thought: "I wish he'd stop asking."
Leo, determined; his thought window shows a calendar with FRIDAY circled — "Friday. I have to do it Friday."
Leo walks away down the hall; grey, grainy, torn SPECULATION panels rise out of Noah (Leo ditching him, laughing behind his back, Noah alone on Friday) — imagined, not real thoughts.
Push into the grey speculation panel until it fills the frame: Leo walking off happily with new friends, Noah left alone ("something terrible").
Over Maya's shoulder: she reaches toward Noah — "Hey, Noah. You okay?" — he's still surrounded by harsh purple thought-noise.
Reverse, over Maya's shoulder: her warm thought "He seems really upset." floats by her head; Noah, arms crossed, avoids her eyes — "I'm fine."
Over Noah's shoulder on Maya, hesitant: "I want to help, but I don't know what to say."
Low angle close-up: Noah snaps "Then don't say ANYTHING!" — the thought-noise shatters and flies off-screen, leaving the frame clean.
Clean, ordinary frame — no overlays at all: Maya, hurt and confused, "...What?" Held for a full beat.
Down the corridor axis behind Noah: Maya walks away and shrinks down the vanishing line ("that's when Noah realized something").
High angle looking down on Noah, alone in the corridor, staring at his open hands (VO: hearing a thought didn't mean he understood it).
Profile close-up: Noah lets his hands drop, eyes lowered ("...didn't mean he understood it").
The week passes in three beats with date chips: TUESDAY Leo turns away from Noah's wave; WEDNESDAY Leo eats alone, on his phone; THURSDAY the clock creeps toward 3:00.
Thursday dusk at the school gate: over Noah's shoulder we watch Leo come down the front steps, only a few metres away ("What was Leo planning to tell him on Friday?").
Leo at the gate, anxious; his thought: "Tomorrow's going to change everything."
Night: Noah lies awake in bed in a shaft of moonlight; the date card flips THURSDAY 11:59 PM → FRIDAY 12:00 AM over a low clock tick.
FRIDAY. Extreme wide of a near-empty courtyard under a cool, overcast sky: Noah waits under the tree, arms crossed; Leo approaches from far away (slow push-in).
The camera creeps closer as Leo reaches Noah; the friends take opposite sides of the frame.
Medium two-shot with a cold band of shadow between them: Noah — "So. What were you gonna tell me?" Leo — "What?"
Over Leo's shoulder (school building behind Noah): Noah, cold — "Don't act like you don't know."
Reverse axis (tree and open courtyard behind Leo), over Noah's shoulder: Leo panics silently; his subdued violet thought sits on his side of frame — "Oh no. Not like this."
The camera tracks around the pair (real parallax): Noah accuses — "You've been hiding something from me all week." Leo pleads — "Noah, just let me explain."
Over Noah's shoulder onto Leo, hands out, pleading: "Noah, just let me explain."
Extreme close-up on Noah's eyes with Leo's thought projected across his face ("He's gonna think I'm abandoning him") — then a pull-back to a close-up as he says it aloud: "So you ARE abandoning me?"
Extreme close-up on Leo: his eyes widen, mouth falls open — "How did you—"
Low-angle medium close-up: Noah jabs a finger — "I KNOW what you're thinking, Leo!"
Silence. The camera pulls back to a wide: a big empty gap of courtyard between the two friends.
Over Noah's shoulder: Leo draws a folded letter out of his bag and holds it out — "I got accepted into a school overseas."
Noah — "...What?" — the anger drains out: his arms drop, his brows relax, and his hand rises to take the letter.
Insert, in Noah's hands: "ASHFORD INTERNATIONAL ACADEMY, London · FULL SCHOLARSHIP (highlighted) · Term begins: Monday, January 11" — the same "A" crest from Leo's laptop.
Wider two-shot with the letter in Noah's hands between them: "And you were just gonna leave without telling me?"
Over Noah's shoulder onto Leo (tree side): "No! I was trying to figure out HOW to tell you."
Leo, earnest and scared; his last violet thought glows then fades away — "Please just be happy for me." (the violet overlays leave the film here).
Profile two-shot against the low golden sun, the letter between them: Noah, quietly — "You said you couldn't keep doing this."
Over Noah's shoulder, sun behind Leo: "Yeah. Pretending everything was normal..." — he looks down, then up.
Profile on Noah looking down at the letter in his hands as Leo finishes ("...while I knew I was leaving"), then up at him: "And you thought I'd hate you?"
Slightly high angle, a slow push from close-up to extreme close-up on Leo, arms wrapped around himself, voice trembling: "I was scared you'd think I chose a new life over being your friend."
A brief warm memory (sepia grade, heavy grain, white flash in and out): Noah and Leo aged 8, laughing, kicking a ball in a golden park.
Back on Leo, relaxed now, head tilted toward Noah, sincere: "I wanted you to be the first person I told."
Silence; only the music. A slow push on Noah: he looks at the letter, blinks, and looks back up at Leo — something shifts.
A continuous push from close-up toward Noah's eyes; his face softens from sad to a small smile ("And suddenly... Noah understood. All day, he'd been hearing people's thoughts.").
Replay, warm and desaturated, back in the hallway: Leo SAID "Yo, you coming over Friday?" while he THOUGHT "He's gonna hate me." ("every passing fear").
Replay in the hallway: Maya SAID "Hey, Noah. You okay?" while she THOUGHT "I want to help, but I don't know what to say." ("every unfinished sentence").
Replay in the classroom: the teacher SAID "What's the answer?" while she THOUGHT "Please don't say C again." ("every private worry, like it was the whole truth").
Noah lowers the letter and looks up at Leo ("He could hear what people were thinking.").
Wide, golden courtyard, no text on screen: the two friends now standing close ("He still didn't know what they meant.").
Noah breaks into a grin: "Dude. You're actually getting a FULL scholarship?" — faint, blurred thought windows still drift in the background; he pays them no attention.
Leo, shy, hand behind his neck: "Yeah." (Noah, off-screen: "That's insane!")
Two-shot, now standing close, with a slow push-in: "Why didn't you just tell me?" — Leo laughs: "I was TRYING to."
Noah, sincere, softly: "...I'm happy for you, man."

THE CHOICE: a small thought window starts to form beside Leo — Noah's eyes flick up to it for a split second, then he looks back at Leo's face and smiles; the window fades away unread as they both laugh.
A small, slightly awkward hug with two back-pats, in medium shot; then the camera slowly pulls out to the wide golden courtyard from the start of Act 3.
Sunset at the school entrance: Noah walks down the steps ("one person he was too scared to ask about").
Noah spots Maya first and walks over; a wordless apology — hand behind his neck, a sheepish half-wave, a silently mouthed "sorry" — and her small forgiving smile.
Over Noah's shoulder: Maya, shy — "Hey. You want to walk home together?" A tiny pink thought starts to form… and fades unread.
Held on Noah's genuine smile — looking at her face, not at any thought — he answers what she SAID: "Yeah. I'd like that."
Wide sunset street: Noah and Maya walk off together toward the sun, silhouetted.
End card over the sunset street (Noah and Maya small in the distance): "What would YOU do if you could hear everyone's thoughts?" with the cast line-up.
